The public TypeScript schema for Hover Popover API.

## Callable destruction contract (0.3.6)

Consumers obtain the existing HoverPopoverApi<TSubject> with useHoverPopovers<TSubject>() beneath HoverPopoverProvider, including beneath EntryPreviewProvider (subject = string). The hook, useCurrentPopoverId and API types are public from the root and /entry; these routes share the same context. The /hover subpath remains DOM-only and does not export React provider hooks. Calling the hook without a provider throws. Capture the API in a descendant effect/ref for external buttons or host callbacks; do not create a second popover manager.

The callable methods return void: dismissSubtree(id) requests the anchor and all descendants; dismissDescendants(id) preserves the anchor and ancestors; dismissAll() requests every live layer. They dispatch reason explicit-api through the provider's dismiss_controller, including frozen targets. cancelUnfrozen(id) requests only unfrozen targets in that subtree and reparents surviving frozen layers. An unknown/removed ID or already-closing target is an idempotent no-op, with no duplicate lease or removal notification. isAlive is false once closing is accepted, even during the fade.

One immutable request snapshots the targets leaf-first. A synchronous controller handler accepts by calling runDefault(); omission vetoes cancelable requests. runDefault is valid only during the handler call and at most once; delayed calls do nothing. Accepted requests reserve targets as closing before lease callbacks, deactivate their generation-safe leases leaf-first, cancel pending open/freeze timers, remove opening previews immediately, and remove visible previews after fadeMs (immediately when zero). Repeated requests do not restart the fade. on_removed is notification-only after physical removal. Consumer exceptions/thenables are contained, not an async destruction protocol.

Owner-unmount cancellation is noncancelable but preserves frozen descendants. Provider unmount bypasses policy, clears all timers and graph/resources, and flushes removal notifications exactly once, including pending and closing layers; it does not dispatch activation deactivation policy. Retained APIs cannot resurrect the disposed provider. No serialized state or schema change is introduced.
